title: Resizing one piece inside a turned card moves the whole card
goal: Turn a card of shapes on a slant, then drag a handle on one piece inside it. That piece resizes as asked, and the rest of the card jumps a few points across the screen at the same time, without anybody touching it. Nothing outside the piece you grabbed should move.
notes:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-20 on a locked Mac with the probe, forced. Walk: Scripts/playtest/turned-piece-walk.json, which draws a 400x200 bar at (300,300) and a 120x60 label at (340,340), groups them, turns the card 20 degrees, then drags the label's top-left handle from (370,289) to (320,250).

Two cut-down copies of that walk, one stopping before the resize and one after, read the on-screen bottomRight corner of BOTH pieces:

  before: "Rectangle" bottomRight on screen (654, 562) / "Rectangle 2" bottomRight on screen (462, 386)
  after:  "Rectangle" bottomRight on screen (653, 566) / "Rectangle 2" bottomRight on screen (462, 390)

Rectangle is the bar. Nothing touched it, and it moved 4 points down the screen.

The arithmetic says why. The group is turned about the centre of its contents' bounds. Before the resize that union is (300,300,400x200), centre (500,400). The resize widens the label leftwards to (279.55,320.61,180.45x79.39), so the union becomes x 279.55 to 700, centre (489.78,400): the pivot everything in the card is turned about slid 10 points left, and every piece in the card swung with it. Rotating the label's own bottomRight (460,400) about (489.78,400) by 20 degrees gives (461.8, 389.8), which is the (462,390) the app reads back.

turned-piece-walk step 38 is the claim that catches it ("the bottom right corner should not have moved at all") and it is RIGHT: the walk is not out of date here, the app is wrong. Step 5 of that walk WAS out of date and is fixed in walks-that-fail-in-the-full-sweep (the rectangle tool hands back to Select after it draws, so the second rectangle needed the tool asking for again); with that fixed the walk reaches 38 and stops there.

The piece-inside-a-turned-card work is a-piece-inside-a-turned-card-moves-on-its-own (done), which took the turn off the POINTER rather than composing it into the frame (PhotonzDocument.uprightPoint in Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerGrouping.swift). This is the other half of the same geometry: a resize changes the contents' bounds, and nothing holds the pivot still while it does.
acceptance: Resizing a piece inside a turned card leaves every other piece in that card exactly where it was on screen, to within half a point
The corner opposite the handle you dragged does not move, on a turned card as well as an upright one
turned-piece-walk passes twice on its own with no further change to the walk

log.note: Confirmed again on 2026-09-20 from the walk sweep work, three runs, identical every time: after the pull the label's drawn bottomRight is (462, 390) where before the pull it is (462, 386), while the label's own document box keeps its opposite corner exactly (280,321 180.4x79.4 has its bottom right at 460.4,400.4 against 460,400 before). So the two answers the app gives about the same corner disagree by 3.5 points. turned-piece-walk now states that claim where it can be read: it reads the drawn bottomRight BEFORE the pull against the very same number the step after the pull claims, so the walk says 'this corner must not move' in one place instead of asserting one absolute number and hoping. The walk stays red until this lands, which is on purpose: it is right and the app is not.
